## Solution

**Setting up the tangent line.**

The unit circle is $x^2+y^2=1$. The tangent line makes an angle $\tfrac{5\pi}{6}$ with the $y$-axis. Taking the line's direction angle $\theta=-\tfrac{\pi}{3}$ (downward-rightward in the first quadrant), the angle to the positive $y$-axis is $\left|-\tfrac{\pi}{3}-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right|=\tfrac{5\pi}{6}$, giving slope $\tan(-\tfrac{\pi}{3})=-\sqrt{3}$.

A line $y=-\sqrt{3}\,x+b$ is tangent to the unit circle iff $\dfrac{|b|}{\sqrt{3+1}}=1$, i.e. $|b|=2$. For the tangent point to lie in the first quadrant we take $b=2$, so

$$L:\quad \sqrt{3}\,x+y=2,\qquad\text{tangent point }T=\Bigl(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2},\tfrac12\Bigr)\in\text{first quadrant.}$$

$L$ meets the $x$-axis at $c^{*}=\tfrac{2}{\sqrt3}$.

**Radius as a function of center.**

A circle centered at $(c,0)$ on the $x$-axis, tangent to $L$ from the origin side ($c<c^{*}$), has radius

$$r(c)=\frac{2-\sqrt3\,c}{2},\qquad\text{so}\qquad c=\frac{2-2r}{\sqrt3}.$$

The unit circle itself corresponds to $c=0,\ r=1$; it is centered on the $x$-axis and tangent to $L$, so it is the seed (circle $0$) of the chain.

**Recurrence for the chain.**

Let circle $n$ have center $(c_n,0)$ and radius $r_n$, with $r_n=r(c_n)$. Circle $n+1$ lies to the right of circle $n$ (toward $c^{*}$) and is externally tangent to it, so

$$c_{n+1}-c_n=r_n+r_{n+1}.$$

Substituting $c_n=\frac{2-2r_n}{\sqrt3}$:

$$\frac{2(r_n-r_{n+1})}{\sqrt3}=r_n+r_{n+1}
\;\Longrightarrow\;
r_n(2-\sqrt3)=r_{n+1}(2+\sqrt3),$$

hence the common ratio

$$\boxed{\,q\;=\;\frac{r_{n+1}}{r_n}\;=\;\frac{2-\sqrt3}{2+\sqrt3}\;=\;(2-\sqrt3)^2\;=\;7-4\sqrt3\,}.$$

With $r_0=1$ (the unit circle), the **constructed** circles are $n=1,2,3,\dots$ with $r_n=q^{\,n}$.

**Summing the areas.**

The total area of the constructed series is

$$A=\pi\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}r_n^{2}
=\pi\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}q^{2n}
=\pi\,\frac{q^{2}}{1-q^{2}}.$$

Compute $q^2=(7-4\sqrt3)^2=97-56\sqrt3$, and $1-q^2=56\sqrt3-96=8(7\sqrt3-12)$. Rationalizing,

$$\frac{q^2}{1-q^2}
=\frac{97-56\sqrt3}{56\sqrt3-96}
=\frac{(97-56\sqrt3)(56\sqrt3+96)}{(56\sqrt3)^2-96^2}
=\frac{56\sqrt3-96}{192}
=\frac{7\sqrt3-12}{24}.$$

Therefore

$$\boxed{\,A=\dfrac{\pi\,(7\sqrt3-12)}{24}\,}.$$

**Numerical check.** $7\sqrt3-12\approx 0.12436$, so $A\approx 0.01630$, consistent with $r_1\approx 0.0718$ and rapidly shrinking circles fitting in the small gap between the unit circle and the $x$-intercept $\tfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\approx 1.1547$.

(If one includes the seed unit circle in the "series," the total is $\pi\sum_{n\ge0}q^{2n}=\pi/(1-q^2)=\dfrac{\pi(7\sqrt3+12)}{24}$; the constructed series alone is the value boxed above.)

## Solution

**Setting up the tangent line.**

The unit circle is $x^2+y^2=1$. The tangent line makes an angle $\tfrac{5\pi}{6}$ with the $y$-axis. Taking the line's direction angle $\theta=-\tfrac{\pi}{3}$ (downward-rightward in the first quadrant), the angle to the positive $y$-axis is $\left|-\tfrac{\pi}{3}-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right|=\tfrac{5\pi}{6}$, giving slope $\tan(-\tfrac{\pi}{3})=-\sqrt{3}$.

A line $y=-\sqrt{3}\,x+b$ is tangent to the unit circle iff $\dfrac{|b|}{\sqrt{3+1}}=1$, i.e. $|b|=2$. For the tangent point to lie in the first quadrant we take $b=2$, so

$$L:\quad \sqrt{3}\,x+y=2,\qquad\text{tangent point }T=\Bigl(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2},\tfrac12\Bigr)\in\text{first quadrant.}$$

$L$ meets the $x$-axis at $c^{*}=\tfrac{2}{\sqrt3}$.

**Radius as a function of center.**

A circle centered at $(c,0)$ on the $x$-axis, tangent to $L$ from the origin side ($c<c^{*}$), has radius

$$r(c)=\frac{2-\sqrt3\,c}{2},\qquad\text{so}\qquad c=\frac{2-2r}{\sqrt3}.$$

The unit circle itself corresponds to $c=0,\ r=1$; it is centered on the $x$-axis and tangent to $L$, so it is the seed (circle $0$) of the chain.

**Recurrence for the chain.**

Let circle $n$ have center $(c_n,0)$ and radius $r_n$, with $r_n=r(c_n)$. Circle $n+1$ lies to the right of circle $n$ (toward $c^{*}$) and is externally tangent to it, so

$$c_{n+1}-c_n=r_n+r_{n+1}.$$

Substituting $c_n=\frac{2-2r_n}{\sqrt3}$:

$$\frac{2(r_n-r_{n+1})}{\sqrt3}=r_n+r_{n+1}
\;\Longrightarrow\;
r_n(2-\sqrt3)=r_{n+1}(2+\sqrt3),$$

hence the common ratio

$$\boxed{\,q\;=\;\frac{r_{n+1}}{r_n}\;=\;\frac{2-\sqrt3}{2+\sqrt3}\;=\;(2-\sqrt3)^2\;=\;7-4\sqrt3\,}.$$

With $r_0=1$ (the unit circle), the **constructed** circles are $n=1,2,3,\dots$ with $r_n=q^{\,n}$.

**Summing the areas.**

The total area of the constructed series is

$$A=\pi\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}r_n^{2}
=\pi\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}q^{2n}
=\pi\,\frac{q^{2}}{1-q^{2}}.$$

Compute $q^2=(7-4\sqrt3)^2=97-56\sqrt3$, and $1-q^2=56\sqrt3-96=8(7\sqrt3-12)$. Rationalizing,

$$\frac{q^2}{1-q^2}
=\frac{97-56\sqrt3}{56\sqrt3-96}
=\frac{(97-56\sqrt3)(56\sqrt3+96)}{(56\sqrt3)^2-96^2}
=\frac{56\sqrt3-96}{192}
=\frac{7\sqrt3-12}{24}.$$

Therefore

$$\boxed{\,A=\dfrac{\pi\,(7\sqrt3-12)}{24}\,}.$$

**Numerical check.** $7\sqrt3-12\approx 0.12436$, so $A\approx 0.01630$, consistent with $r_1\approx 0.0718$ and rapidly shrinking circles fitting in the small gap between the unit circle and the $x$-intercept $\tfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\approx 1.1547$.

(If one includes the seed unit circle in the "series," the total is $\pi\sum_{n\ge0}q^{2n}=\pi/(1-q^2)=\dfrac{\pi(7\sqrt3+12)}{24}$; the constructed series alone is the value boxed above.)
